messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV_CACHE_EVICT_BURST on prod-us-west-1 at 2026-03-15T02:00:34Z — latency and 5xx spikes detected
oncall_tony: seeing token cadence drops + 502s from streaming proxies, paging now
maya_sre: paging @ravi_eng, tagging eng-runtime
ravi_eng: I'm awake, looking. Any recent rollout?
maya_sre: no manual deploys; autoscaler did a rebalancing ~t-6m
julie_ml: load shows continuous_batch_size jumped for many workers, KV cache size ballooned to ~1.2TB on a few nodes
oncall_tony: attaching quick logs -> https://dash.redwood.ai/d/abcd/kvcache?from=now-15m
ravi_eng: running `kubectl exec -n runtime -- curl http://localhost:8080/metrics | grep kv_cache` now
ravi_eng: metrics: kv_cache_items_total=4.1e8, kv_cache_bytes=1298473568000, continuous_batch_inflight=420
maya_sre: streaming queues show partial flush timeouts, token cadence going down to ~0.3 tokens/s on affected hosts
oncall_tony: impact: Customer-A/B experiencing streaming stalls and truncated responses; Customer-C seeing higher latency on embeddings
amy_cs: CS: Customer A opened a P1 ticket, chat sessions timing out — they're escalating to their ops team
ravi_eng: hypothesis: regression in continuous batching logic allowed runaway batch growth when prefix reuse high -> cache miss amplification + eviction pressure
maya_sre: mitigation plan (short): 1) throttle continuous_batch_max_size to 64 2) enable aggressive KV eviction TTL temporarily 3) roll back batch-tuning config if present
ravi_eng: applying config patch via config-service to canaries now:
```
PATCH /v1/configs/runtime/batching
{\"continuous_batch_max_size\":64,\"kv_eviction_ttl_secs\":3600}
```
ravi_eng: patch applied to prod-us-west-1 canaries (2/4)
oncall_tony: observability: watching continuous_batch_inflight, kv_cache_bytes, streaming_partial_flush_count
maya_sre: dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/efgh/streaming-cadence?from=now-30m
ravi_eng: canary metrics stabilizing, kv_cache_bytes falling ~15% after eviction TTL kicked in
julie_ml: perf: p95 streaming latency on canaries down from ~3.8s -> ~1.1s
oncall_tony: proceeding to roll out config patch region-wide with 30s stagger and healthchecks
oncall_tony: rollout started
incident-bot: DEPLOYMENT: config-service PATCH applied by ravi_eng at 2026-03-15T02:04:12Z
maya_sre: mid-rollout alert: one node hit OOM during eviction, pod restarted and replaced; investigating memory churn
ravi_eng: paused rollout after churn — digging into eviction memory path for leak or high tail allocations
ravi_eng: emergency workaround: reduce continuous_batch_max_size further to 32 on the problematic pool
ravi_eng: applied emergency change to pool-prod-us-west-1-2
ravi_eng: memory pressure dropped, no further OOMs observed
oncall_tony: resuming rollout with new conservative values: pool-prod-us-west-1-2 at 32, others at 64
amy_cs: preparing customer comms: drafting banner for Customer A + proactive email to top affected accounts
amy_cs: suggested language: \"We observed temporary streaming stalls affecting some chat sessions. A mitigation is in place and full service is restored for most customers; we will follow up with a post-incident summary.\" :+1:
julie_ml: next dev work: capture sample requests that caused huge batch formation and add runtime guardrail to cap batch growth purely on tokens, not just requests
ravi_eng: filed RN-2048: \"runtime: guardrail to prevent runaway continuous batches\" assigned eng-runtime
maya_sre: oncall handoff in 30m to @tone_nightshift — leaving runbook notes and command history in the incident tracker
oncall_tony: ack, will monitor overnight and keep dashboards pinned
amy_cs: CS will send a targeted update after final confirmation in 15m
ravi_eng: closing loop: current metrics look stable; streaming_partial_flush_count trending to 0 across region
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Severity changed Sev2 -> Sev3 at 2026-03-15T02:36:00Z — mitigation successful
maya_sre: handoff note: next_oncall=@tone_nightshift, runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/kvcache-eviction, key alerts to keep: kv_cache_bytes > 900GB, continuous_batch_inflight > 200, streaming_partial_flush_count > 5
tone_nightshift: ack — will enable a temporary alert for kv_cache_bytes and keep a tight pager policy
amy_cs: will send final customer note in 1h if no regression, prepping details for affected orgs
ravi_eng: postmortem owners: eng-runtime (ravi_eng), eng-ml (julie_ml), sre (maya_sre), cs (amy_cs)
maya_sre: ETA for first postmortem draft: 48h; include root cause attempts, timeline, customer impact, mitigations, and follow-ups
oncall_tony: leaving detailed notes and exact CLI history in the incident tracker for the oncall handoff
END
